paragraphs.text: Ricky: Hi. I’m Ricky Raccoon. Welcome to my house.
Rachel: And I’m Rachel, Ricky’s sister.
Ricky: Yes, she is my baby sister. Come in and meet my parents.
Rachel: I’m not a baby, Ricky!
Ricky: There’s my dad. He’s a computer programmer. Hello, Dad!
Dad: Hi, Ricky. Play nicely with your sister.
Ricky: There’s my mom. She is a dentist. Hi, Mom.
Mom: Hello, Ricky! Dinner will be ready soon.
Ricky: Come on. Let’s go upstairs. I will show you my room.
Rachel: Ricky, where are you? Let’s play a game.
Ricky: This is my room. I like baseball.
This is my fish. His name is Gill.
My sister’s room is down the hall. Let’s go see.
Rachel: I’m right here, Ricky!
Ricky: Okay, Rachel. What do you want to play?
Rachel: Let’s play house!
Ricky: Mom, where can I put this?
Mom: Put it on the Christmas tree.
Ricky: Look at me! I’m a Christmas tree!
Rachel: Be careful!
Dad: Finally, it is finished. Ricky, plug in the lights.
Ricky: Okay, Dad! Here it goes. Wow! They look beautiful.
Dad: Ricky, Rachel, did you write to Santa?
Ricky: Not yet, Dad. I want to email Santa.
Rachel: Me too!
Ricky: Don’t copy me, Rachel!
Dad: Ricky, be nice. Help Rachel use the computer.
Ricky: "Dear Santa, I want a flying hat, a giant power robot, and a bike."
Rachel: That’s too much, Ricky.
Ricky: Don’t bother me! Wait a minute. What do you want for Christmas?
Rachel: I want a doll, and a dress, and a tea set, and a scarf, and . . .
Ricky: Slow down! You are talking too fast.
Rachel: . . . a hat! That’s everything.
Ricky: And finally, "santa@northpole.org." Send.
Rachel: Merry Christmas, Ricky.
Ricky: Merry Christmas, Rachel.
Rachel: Can we open our presents?
Ricky: No, we can’t. I have an idea. Let’s make breakfast.
Rachel: That sounds fun! Ricky, we don’t know how to cook.
Ricky: Don’t worry. We can use the toaster and the microwave. Oh no, the toast is burning.
Rachel: Ricky, the microwave.
Mom: It’s six o’clock in the morning. What are you doing?
Ricky: We are making breakfast. Sorry, Mom.
Rachel: Me too, sorry!
Dad: That’s okay. Let’s open the presents first.
Ricky & Rachel: Hurray!
Rachel: This one is for you, Ricky.
Ricky: Here’s one for you, Rachel. Wow! I like it!
Rachel: It’s the doll I wanted!
Ricky & Rachel: This is for you, Mom and Dad!
Mom & Dad: Thank you! They are beautiful!
Everyone: Merry Christmas, everyone!
Mom: Rachel. What day is it today?
Rachel: It’s December 31st.
Mom: That’s right. What day is tomorrow?
Rachel: It’s the first day of the new year.
Mom: That’s correct. It will be the year 2006. What do you want to do in the new year?
Ricky: I want to fly.
Rachel: Hee-hee! Ricky, flying is impossible.
Mom: Okay, Rachel. What do you want to do in the new year?
Rachel: I’ll be good to my brother.
Ricky: Thanks, sis!
Father: Come on, everyone. It’s almost time.
Ricky: Wow! What are they doing?
Father: They are counting down to the new year.
TV Announcer: 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 . . .
Everyone: . . . 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Happy New Year! Happy New Year, everyone!
Ricky: Wow! Look at all the snow! Mom, can I play outside?
Mom: After breakfast, Ricky.
Brian: Hello. This is Brian Rabbit!
Ricky: Hey, Brian. It’s Ricky. I’m going to the park. Can you come?
Brian: Yes, I can. See you there.
Brenda: Hey, Ricky! What are you doing?
Ricky: Hi, Brenda. I’m making a snow angel. It’s fun. You should try. Let’s go to the park. We can make a snowman.
Brenda: Great!
Ricky: Good to see you, Brian. Let’s build a snowman.
Brian: Okay, Ricky.
Brenda: What are you doing, Ricky?
Ricky: Watch and see. This snowball will get super big!
Brenda: Ricky, are you okay?
Ricky: Brrrrr! I’m okay, just a little cold.
Brian: Don’t do that again! The snowman needs something . . .
Ricky: I have an idea. But I have to run home. Just wait a minute.
Rachel: Ricky, where are you going? That’s my hat and scarf!
Ricky: I have to go.
Brian: Great, Ricky! Where did you get those?
Ricky: He-he! They’re Rachel’s. The snowman needs to be warm.
Brenda: Two raisins for the eyes . . . and a few for the mouth.
Ricky: And a carrot for the nose. Where is the carrot?
Ricky: I put it right there. Brian? Where are you?
Brian: He-he . . . Sorry guys! Carrots are my favorite.
Ricky: Give me the carrot, Brian.
Brenda: It looks great!
Brian: Ewww! Ricky, what are you eating?
Ricky: I’m thirsty. This snow is good.
Brian: Did you hear that?
Ricky: Hear what? Eat some snow, Brian.
Brian: Ouch!
Ricky: It’s Spike and Hopper! Everyone, hide.
Brenda: Brian, are you okay?
Brian: I think so, but that hurt.
Brenda: What do those bullies want?
Ricky: I don’t know. But let’s get ready.
Brian: Are you ready, Ricky? Snowball fight!
Hopper: Spike, are you okay?
Spike: Who threw that? You are in big trouble!
Hopper: Yeah! You’re in big trouble now.
Brenda: What are we going to do?
Ricky: Wait a minute. I have a plan.
Hopper: Spike, are you okay?
Spike: Hopper! I am fine.
Brenda: We want a truce.
Spike: No truce! This is war.
Ricky: Okay. Here comes my secret weapon.
Spike: Ha-ha-ha! Way to go, Ricky! Now you can have a truce.
All: Are you okay?
Ricky: I’m okay. Oh well, at least they’re gone.
Mom: Ricky, wake up. It’s time to get up.
Ricky: I don’t want to get up. I want to sleep more.
Mom: Get up, Ricky. We have to go.
Ricky: Can I stay home, Mom?
Mom: No, Ricky. Your father has a meeting today. He can’t stay home.
Ricky: I don’t want to go. Your office is boring!
Mom: Ricky Raccoon, get up and get ready now!
Ricky: Okay! I’m getting up.
Ricky: Woo-hoo! Toys!
Mom: Sorry, guys. Those toys are for patients. You have to stay in my office.
Ricky: That’s not fair, Mom! Your office is not fun.
Rachel: Mom, Ricky pushed me!
Mom: Follow me. I have a surprise for you.
Ricky: Wow! Lego blocks.
Rachel: And a dollhouse. Thanks, Mom!
Mom: Go and open the freezer, Ricky!
Ricky: Is this for us, Mom?
Mom: Yes, it’s for you. But not until after lunch─if you’re good!
Ricky: Thanks, Mom. We’ll be good.
Ricky: I’m bored.
Rachel: Mom said to stay here, Ricky. What can you see?
Rachel: Mom said to stay here, Ricky.
Ricky: Come on, Rachel. Mom won’t know. The hall is empty.
Timothy: W-w-who are y-y-you?
Ricky: I’m Ricky Raccoon. This is my sister, Rachel.
Rachel: What’s wrong?
Timothy: I have a t-t-toothache. I-I don’t l-l-like the dentist.
Rachel: Don’t worry. The dentist is our mom. She’s nice.
Ricky: Hey, guys! Watch me! I’m a fountain.
Timothy: Ha-ha-ha! You’re funny.
Ricky: See, the dentist isn’t scary. It’s fun!
Rachel: Ricky, what are you doing?
Ricky: Hold on! Here we go!
Timothy: This is fun!
Mom: What is going on here?
Ricky: Sorry, Mom. I guess we can’t have ice cream now.
Timothy: Don’t be angry, Dr. Raccoon. I was scared. But Ricky and Rachel cheered me up.
Mom: You can have ice cream after lunch. Thank you for helping Timothy. Here’s a treat.
Rachel & Ricky: Bye, Timothy! We have to go.
Brian: Ricky, what are you doing?
Ricky: I’m going to practice flying.
Brian: You can’t fly, Ricky!
Ricky: Not yet, but soon!
Brian: Hi, Rachel. Want to play?
Ricky: One, two, three, go!
Brian: Ricky, are you okay?
Rachel: Be careful, Ricky.
Ricky: Maybe I need to climb higher.
Rachel: You can’t fly, Ricky!
Brian: Oh no! Here comes Veronica Fox.
Veronica: Hello, Richard. How are you?
Rachel: Richard? Who’s Richard?
Ricky: H-hi, Veronica. I’m f-f-fine, thank you.
Brian: Hi, Veronica.
Veronica: I didn’t say hi to you, Brian! I don’t talk to people in ugly clothes.
Rachel: I like Brian’s clothes.
Veronica: Bye, Richard. I hope I see you later.
Brian: She’s mean. Why didn’t you say something, Ricky.
Ricky: Oh-oh! Guys, could you help me? That was fun. I want to try again!
Brian & Rachel: You can’t fly, Ricky!
Rachel: Happy Valentine's Day, Ricky! I love you!
Ricky: Thanks, Rachel. I love you too. I'll give you your card later. Bye.
Brenda: Hi, Ricky! Happy Valentine's Day!
Ricky: Thanks, Brenda! You too.
Brenda: What's that, Ricky? Is it for me?
Ricky: Umm . . . no. Sorry, Brenda, I have to go.
Brian: Happy Valentine's Day. This is for you, Brenda.
Brenda: Thank you, Brian. This is for you.
Brian: Why are you sad? Don't you like chocolates?
Brenda: It's not that. Ricky doesn't like me.
Brian: Yes, he does. And I like you too.
Brenda: Thanks, Brian. I am happy you're my friend.
Veronica: Hello, Richard! What are you doing here?
Ricky: Hello, Veronica. H-happy V-valentine's Day.
Veronica: Thank you, Richard! Happy Valentine's Day to you.
Ricky: This is for you. I have to go. Bye!
Father: Ricky, school is starting again soon. Are you excited?
Ricky: I am excited and nervous.
Rachel: Why are you nervous, Ricky? School will be fun.
Ricky: How do you know? You haven't been to school yet!
Rachel: I went to preschool! It's always fun.
Ricky: Preschool is all playtime. You don't have to study.
Father: That's enough, you two. Ricky, what do you need for school? Let's make a list.
Ricky: I need sour candy, lots of sour candy. And a book bag and roller rocket shoes. Then I can move around quickly.
Father: Ricky, rocket shoes aren't real. And they aren't needed for school. I think you need pencils and notebooks.
Ricky: How will I get to school without rocket shoes?
Father: By walking, Ricky!
Rachel: I need scissors and glue, Dad.
Ricky: And a baby carriage to ride to school.
Father: That's enough, you guys. Great lists! We'll go shopping tomorrow.
Ricky: Rachel, what are you doing?
Rachel: I'm making a classroom. Let's play school, Ricky.
Ricky: I don't want to play school!
Rachel: Hello! I'm Mrs. Raccoon. Ricky, please take your seat.
Rachel: Welcome to your first day of school! Do you have any questions?
Ricky: No. No one has any questions.
Rachel: Good. Take out your books, please. Read pages 4 to 7. Write a ten-page story. Tell me why your sister is great.
Dad: You two, go and find pencils. I will get the scissors and glue.
Ricky & Rachel: Okay, Dad.
Dad: Ricky, take care of your sister.
Ricky: Excuse me. Where are the pencils?
Salesperson: In aisle 13.
Ricky & Rachel: Thank you!
Rachel: Wow! Look at all the pencils.
Ricky: Dad said we can spend three dollars on pencils.
Rachel: Wow! Look at this.
Ricky: That’s nice, Rachel. But we can only spend three dollars.
Rachel: How many pencils can we buy?
Ricky: We can buy six pencils. Hey! I wanted to choose them. We got the pencils, Dad.
Dad: Good job. Do you like this book bag?
Ricky: Super Power Squirrel! Wow! Thanks, Dad!
Salesperson: Did you find everything you need?
Rachel: Yes, we did. Thank you!
Salesperson: Your total is forty-two dollars and fifty-two cents.
Ricky: I can’t wait for school to start! Look at me. I’m Super Power Squirrel!
Dad: Now he’s excited!
Mom: Hurry up! It’s almost time to go.
Ricky: I’m ready, Mom!
Mom: Ricky! Go back upstairs and change, please.
Dad: Ricky, how are you doing?
Ricky: Just a minute.
Dad: Are you ready to go?
Ricky: I think so, Dad.
Dad: Do you have your pencil case and notebook?
Ricky: Yes, Dad. I just packed them.
Dad: Okay. Let’s go.
Mom: Rachel, are you ready?
Rachel: I need help, Mom. I don’t know what to wear.
Mom: That bow is too big, Rachel. Let’s try a different one.
Rachel: It’s my first day. I want to look pretty.
Mom: You will, Rachel. Don’t worry. How does that look?
Rachel: I look pretty, Mom. Thank you!
Ricky: Finally! I hope you’re faster tomorrow.
Mom: Good-bye, you guys! Have a great day at school.
All: Bye, Mom!
Rachel: Dad, what's my new teacher like?
Father: She's very kind and friendly. She was Ricky's kindergarten teacher.
Crossing guard: Good morning, Ricky! How are you today?
Ricky: I'm fine, thank you. Dad, Rachel! Come on!
Father: Hello, Mrs. Kitty! It's nice to see you again.
Crossing guard: It's nice to see you too, Mr. Raccoon. What's your name, sweetie?
Rachel: My name is Rachel. It's my first day of school!
Ricky: Come on! Let's go!
Crossing guard: Don't cross the road without me, Ricky!
Ricky: Yes, Mrs. Kitty.
Rachel: What's that sign for?
Crossing guard: This sign tells the cars to stop.
Ricky: It also tells you to stop asking questions.
Father: Ricky, we have lots of time. Don't worry! Okay, you guys, let's cross the street. Always wait for Mrs. Kitty to tell you it's safe to cross.
Ricky: I know, Dad. I did this last year. Bye, Dad! Bye, Rachel! See you later.
Father: Good-bye, Ricky. Have a nice day.
Father: I will take you to your class now. When school is finished, I will come back to pick you up.
Rachel: Okay, Dad!
Father: Here we go.
Ricky: Hi, guys!
All friends: Hi, Ricky!
Brian: Cool book bag, Ricky! Super Power Squirrel is the best.
Ricky: Thanks, Brian. My dad bought it for me.
Brenda: What's in the bag, Ricky?
Ricky: You'll see. Just wait a minute.
Veronica: What is it, Ricky?
Ricky: Super sour candy, of course.
Brian: It's pretty sour, Ricky.
Mr. Brown: Good morning! What do you have there, Ricky?
Ricky: Nothing, Mr. Brown.
Mr. Brown: Come on, Ricky. Show me, please.
Ricky: It's candy, sir. Would you like some?
Mr. Brown: Maybe . . .
Mr. Brown: No . . . candy . . . in class, Ricky. Put it away please.
Ricky: Yes, Mr. Brown. I won't bring candy to class again.
Mr. Brown: Okay, everyone, close your books and go outside for recess.
All: Whoo-hoo!
Brian: Let's play Peter Pan and Captain Hook.
Brenda: Okay, I get to be Tinker Bell.
Veronica: That's a dumb game. You guys play. I'm going to watch.
Brian: Okay, Brenda. Then I am Captain Hook. You're captured, Tinker Bell.
Ricky: I'm Peter Pan. Everyone, get on board Captain Hook's ship.
Brenda: Save me, Peter Pan! Captain Hook has locked me in his ship.
Ricky: Don't worry, Tinker Bell! I'll save you!
Brian: I don't think so, Peter Pan. This time there is no escape.
Brian: Peter Pan! Today, you will lose!
Ricky: I'll never lose to you, Captain Hook! And I'll save Tinker Bell.
Brian: Nooooo! I'll get you, Peter Pan!
Ricky: Come on, Tinker Bell. Let's get out of here!
Brenda: Peter Pan, you're my hero!
Ricky: Okay, okay, Brenda. The game is over. Brian, are you hurt?
Brian: I'm fine. This sand is comfortable.
Brenda: Come on, you guys. Recess is over.
Ricky: I'm Captain Hook next recess.
Rachel: Mom, where is Grandma going?
Mom: She is going to visit a friend in Forestwood.
Rachel: Why are we visiting her then?
Ricky: Because we have to pick up her dog.
Ricky & Rachel: Hi, Grandma!
Grandma: Hello, my darlings. It’s so nice to see you.
Ricky: Hello, Bingo!
Rachel: I want to play too.
Grandma: Ricky, Rachel! Come inside for cookies and milk.
Rachel: It’s nice to see you too, Bingo.
Dad: How long will you be gone?
Grandma: I’ll be gone for two weeks. This is Bingo’s food. He gets fed twice a day. I take him for a walk in the evening.
Ricky: Can I feed him now?
Grandma: Yes. But not too much, Ricky.
Rachel: Bingo! Come here, Bingo. I want to play with you.
Grandma: Bingo! Bad dog!
Ricky: Rachel! Don’t bother the dog.
Rachel: He-he-he! Sorry, Ricky.
Mother: Okay, everyone. Listen to me, please. I've made a dog-care schedule.
Rachel: A dog-care schedule?
Mother: It tells us who feeds and walks the dog.
Ricky: Shhh! Bingo, this is about you.
Mother: Ricky will feed Bingo in the morning. And Rachel will do it at night.
Ricky & Rachel: Okay, Mom.
Mother: Monday to Friday, Ricky will walk Bingo in the evenings. On the weekends, your father or I will do it.
Rachel: I want to walk the dog too.
Father: I'm sorry, Rachel. You are too young, but you can help your brother.
Ricky: I don't need any help!
Father: Ricky, be nice to your sister. She wants to walk Bingo too.
Ricky: Yes, Dad. She can help.
Mother: Why don't you take the dog for a walk now?
Ricky: Okay, Mom.
Rachel: Me too, me too!
Ricky: Rachel, throw this ball as far as you can. Bingo and I are going to have a race.
Rachel: Yeah! Bingo won! Bingo won!
Rachel: I'm bored, Ricky. It's raining too much.
Ricky: It's raining because it's spring. It always rains in the spring.
Rachel: Why?
Ricky: It rains because the flowers need water to grow.
Rachel: Even Bingo is bored.
Ricky: Come on, Rachel. Let's play outside. Put on your raincoat.
Rachel: Ricky, take an umbrella.
Ricky: I don't need an umbrella. It's not raining that hard. Maybe I do need an umbrella.
Rachel: He-he! Here you go. Look, Ricky. It's a little river in our backyard.
Ricky: This is fun! Come on in, Rachel. I wish we had little boats.
Rachel: Just a minute, Ricky.
Ricky: Cool, Rachel! Where did you get the boats?
Rachel: We made them in kindergarten.
Ricky: Thanks, Rachel! Let's race. Ready, Rachel? One, two, three, go!
Rachel: Woo-hoo! Ricky, this is fun! Can we race again?
Rachel: When is Grandma going to get here?
Dad: Be patient, Rachel. She will be here soon.
Ricky & Rachel: Welcome home, Grandma! We missed you!
Grandma: Hello, my dears. I missed you too.
Ricky: How was your trip?
Grandma: It was wonderful, Ricky. I had a lot of fun. My baby! Hello. I have missed you!
Ricky: I walked him every day, Grandma.
Rachel: I helped.
Grandma: Thanks. Who wants a present?
Ricky & Rachel: I do. I do!
Ricky: Wow, a real Indian headdress! I can’t wait to wear it to school.
Rachel: A beautiful doll! Thank you, Grandma.
Ricky: Help me! He wants to eat the feathers.
Grandma: Bingo! Come here, now! Ricky, are you okay?
Ricky: Yes, I am. But my hat is messed up.
Grandma: Ricky, I’m very sorry.
Ricky: Since mine is wrecked, can I have another gift?
Mom: What do you want to plant this year?
Rachel: I want to plant strawberries.
Mom: That's great, Rachel. What do you want to plant, Ricky?
Ricky: It's a secret, Mom.
Dad: Okay, you guys. Everyone, grab a shovel. First, we need to plant the seeds. Plant your seeds in straight lines.
Rachel: Okay, Dad!
Ricky: Soon, I will have a chocolate-covered-raisin tree. Then, I will climb the tree and eat chocolate-covered raisins all day.
Mom: Ricky, are you planting your seeds?
Ricky: Yes, Mom! I was just thinking about something.
Rachel: This is hard work, Dad.
Dad: Yes, it is. You are doing a good job, Rachel. Your strawberries will grow well.
Mom: Ricky, what did you plant?
Ricky: You'll see!
Rachel: Wow, Ricky! Look at my little strawberry plants.
Ricky: That's nice, Rachel. Go and turn on the water, please.
Rachel: But Mom just watered the garden.
Ricky: I know, Rachel. But mine need more water.
Rachel: Ricky, that's too much water.
Ricky: Okay, Rachel! Turn off the water!
Rachel: Ricky, what kind of seeds are those?
Ricky: Never mind. I need some blankets. My seeds need to be warm. Now, they will grow.
Rachel: Ricky, here comes Mom.
Mom: Ricky, what are you doing with the blankets?
Ricky: I need to keep my seeds warm. My seeds aren't growing, Mom.
Mom: Ricky, what kind of seeds did you plant?
Ricky: I planted chocolate-covered raisins.
Mom: That's okay, Ricky. Let's clean up and get you some real seeds.
Ricky: Thanks, Mom. Can you find lollipop seeds for me?
Rachel: When is your birthday, Ricky?
Ricky: It's this Saturday, May 20th.
Father: What do you want to do for your birthday, Ricky? Do you want to have a party?
Ricky: Yes, I do. I want to invite all my friends. And I want Super Power Squirrel to come!
Father: That might be difficult, Ricky. I'll check if he's available.
Ricky: Thanks, Dad! I know you can do it.
Father: Well, Ricky, what presents do you want for your birthday?
Ricky: Hmmm, let me think . . .
Father: Ricky. Ricky! Rickeeeeey!! Did you hear my question?
Ricky: Sorry, Dad. Yes, I heard you. I want kangaroo shoes.
Rachel: Ricky, what present can I get you?
Ricky: Don't worry, Rachel. I know you don't have any money.
Rachel: I know! I saw it on TV. I can bake you a cake.
Ricky: Oh no!
All: Surprise! Happy birthday, Ricky!
Ricky: Wow! Everybody is here!
Brian: We wanted to surprise you.
Veronica: This is for you, Richard.
Ricky: Th-th-thank you, V-veronica.
Brian: Walkie-talkies! Cool!
Veronica: They are not for you, Brian! One is for Richard and one is for me.
Ricky: Who is it?
Super Power Squirrel: I'm a friend of your father. Happy birthday, Ricky!
Ricky: Father did it. Woo-hoo! Super Power Squirrel came to my party!
Super Power Squirrel: I can't stay long, Ricky. I have to protect the world. Have a very happy birthday and play safely.
Ricky: Thank you, Super Power Squirrel. My dad knows Super Power Squirrel.
Brenda: That was cool, Ricky! Open the box. Wow! Ricky! Put on your kangaroo shoes.
Ricky: Watch this, guys! One, two, three . . . I guess I need to practice first.
Mom: Let's go to the playroom. It's time to play a game.
Ricky: What game will we play?
Mom: We're going to play "hit the piñata." Who wants to go first?
All: Me. Me. I do. I do.
Mom: Ricky, it's your birthday. You pick the first player.
Ricky: I pick Brian.
Brian: Where is it?
Mom: Good hit, Brian. Who's next, Ricky?
Ricky: My turn, Mom. I don't need a stick. I'm going to do a taekwondo kick.
Mom: Be careful, Ricky. Good try. You choose who is next.
Ricky: I choose Brenda.
Brenda: Here I go!
Rachel: Happy birthday, Ricky! I made these for you.
Ricky: What are they?
Rachel: They are your favorite snack: Twinkies. I decorated them.
Ricky: They look good. Thank you, Rachel.
All: Happy birthday, Ricky!
Mom: It's Saturday, everyone. Here is a list of chores.
Ricky: Chores? I hate chores.
Dad: Today will be different, Ricky. Today you will get an allowance.
Rachel: What's an allowance?
Ricky: It's money that you earn by doing chores.
Mom: I want both of you to make your beds. Then you can collect the garbage, Ricky.
Ricky: I'm going to start right now. Let's work together. It will be quicker.
Rachel: Okay, Ricky. Let's make your bed first.
Ricky: Grab that corner, Rachel. I'll take this one. Flap it in the air.
Rachel: That was easy. Let's do my bed.
Ricky: I'm going to use my wagon. You push and I'll steer.
Rachel: You're heavy, Ricky!
Ricky: Okay, I'll help. Whew!
Mom: Ricky Raccoon, clean up this mess right now!
Ricky: Sorry, Mom.
Rachel: I'll help, Ricky.
Ricky: Thanks, Rachel. I will share my allowance with you.
Ricky: Dad, I don't feel very well.
Dad: Oh my! I think you have a fever. Go back to bed, Ricky. You shouldn't go to school today.
Ricky: Yes, Dad.
Rachel: Can I stay home to take care of Ricky?
Dad: No, you have to go to school. Have something to eat, Ricky. I'm going downstairs. Call me if you need anything.
Ricky: Okay, Dad. Dad!
Dad: What do you need, son?
Ricky: A glass of water, please. Dad! Dad! Dad!
Dad: He must be feeling better. That's the tenth time he has called. Are you feeling better, Ricky?
Ricky: Ohh, I feel worse.
Dad: Go to sleep, then. I'm going to have an ice-cream sundae.
Ricky: Wait! I think I feel better now.
Dad: Ricky Raccoon, you were pretending. Shame on you!
Ricky: Sorry, Dad. I really was sick this morning. Can I have some ice cream? I feel better now.
Dad: Come on!
Ricky: Brian, let's ride our bikes after school.
Brian: Sure. We can go─ouch!
Mr. Brown: Brian and Ricky! Turn around, please.
Brian & Ricky: Yes, Mr. Brown.
Ricky: They always get us into trouble.
Brian: Yeah, it's not fair. What are you doing, Ricky?
Ricky: I have a plan. Make some paper balls. Ready, Brian?
Brian: Be careful! I don't want to get into trouble.
Spike: I'm going to get you, Ricky!
Mr. Brown: Do you have something to say, Spike?
Spike: No, Mr. Brown. I'm sorry. Hey, Ricky.
Mr. Brown: Did you throw this, Spike?
Spike: Y-y-yes, b-b-but . . .
Mr. Brown: No "buts," Spike. You will clean the blackboard after school. And you can help him, Hopper.
Brian: We're going to the space museum.
Ricky: I’ve been waiting for this trip all year.
Brian: He-he. Maybe you'll get a chance to fly.
Ricky: Someday I will fly.
Mr. Brown: Ricky, don't stand up in the bus, please.
Ricky: Sorry, Mr. Brown.
Mr. Brown: Welcome to the space museum. Follow me, please. Put on a space suit, everyone.
Ricky: Hey Brian, come with me.
Brian: We're going to get into trouble, Ricky.
Ricky: Don't worry, Brian.
Brian: Wow!
